problem: Existing 3DGS real-to-sim pipelines mostly take monocular video (slow scanning of large scenes), and separate foreground objects either by scanning them separately or by segmenting directly in 3D Gaussian space, which gives poor boundaries, holes and bad inpainting.
motivation: Embodied policy training needs simulation environments with low sim-to-real gap, decoupled manipulable objects and collision geometry, built quickly from real scans. Gaussians straddle object boundaries, so 3D-space segmentation is unreliable, while 2D segmentation and inpainting are mature.
key_idea: Extract objects and inpaint the background in the 2D image domain across multiple panoramic-camera video streams (using camera poses and point-cloud projection plus SAM3/SAM2), then reconstruct the background with 3DGS plus a mesh and generate objects with multi-view TRELLIS for import into Isaac Sim.
insight: Segmenting in 2D and inpainting before 3D reconstruction gives cleaner boundaries than 3D Gaussian segmentation methods (LERF mIoU 93-96 vs best baseline ~78-89). The ablation shows that projecting the 3D point cloud into every frame using COLMAP poses and combining it with SAM2/SAM3 tracking extracts more frames than either alone (e.g. bar 67.49 vs 52.37 / 49.80), and that SAM3 tracking runs out of memory on large multi-stream scenes.
method: Multi-stream capture: 1-3 Insta360 X5 panoramic cameras, each video split into 2-5 viewpoints, with camera poses and sparse point cloud recovered via Postshot/COLMAP.

Pose-based localization: the user picks a mask on one frame (SAM3 with text or click); the object's 3D points are projected into every frame with extrinsics/intrinsics, depth-filtered for occlusion (z <= D+tau), and the smallest mask containing the most projected points is chosen.
SAM2 propagation: fills frames missed by projection (scale changes, partial views) by propagating masks within each stream from the first frame that has a result mask.
2D inpainting: remove masked objects and inpaint all images with LaMa, and delete the corresponding points from the point cloud.

Background reconstruction: 3DGS via gsplat on inpainted images, expected-depth rendering, TSDF fusion + Poisson (or TSDF zero-level-set mesh with hole filling for small scenes) for collision mesh, converted for Isaac Sim with 3DGRUT.

Object generation: select the top masks by a weighted score (area, fill ratio, center prior, boundary cut, aspect ratio, resolution) with a minimum frame gap d, then feed them to multi-view TRELLIS to produce meshes.

setting.backbone: SAM3 + SAM2 + LaMa + TRELLIS + 3DGS (gsplat), all pretrained/frozen pipeline components; downstream policies Pi0.5 (manipulation) and Uni-NaVid (navigation)
setting.training_data: Reconstruction is per-scene optimization (30k iterations 3DGS). Downstream policies: 50 sim / 50 real demos per manipulation task (Pi0.5); simulated navigation data for Uni-NaVid finetuning (100 samples per task).
setting.observation: Multi-view panoramic camera-array video streams (RGB) with SfM camera poses and sparse point cloud
setting.action_space: Manipulation: robot arm (Piper) actions via Pi0.5; navigation: Uni-NaVid low-level actions on Kitt 15 robot

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark results. Reported results are on LERF segmentation, a custom sundries inpainting scene, and real-robot success rates (Uni-NaVid navigation in custom bar/wework scenes: 3 tasks, zero-shot-in-real 75/0/100, sim2sim 83.33/66.67/50, sim2real 100/100/100), none of which match the canonical benchmark list.
results: On LERF, GASE gets mIoU 93.32/95.63/95.91 (figurines/ramen/teatime), beating LangSplat, Gaussian Grouping and ObjectGS by over 10% on average, and it has the best inpainting PSNR 27.09 vs 26.22 (Gaussian Grouping). Sim-trained policies reach >60% real-robot success on manipulation (sim2real 0.73/0.60/0.67 vs real2real 0.73/0.67/0.67), and simulated training raises Uni-NaVid navigation success on the real robot over its zero-shot performance in two of three tasks (e.g. fire extinguisher 0 to 100).
limitations: Depends on vision-based SfM (COLMAP/Postshot), which is slow for multi-stream scenes, gives sparse point clouds and can lose camera viewpoints; feed-forward alternatives (VGGT, DA3, Pi3) were noticeably worse on PSNR/LPIPS.
2D-domain separation is not real-time: extracting a new object requires rerunning the whole pipeline.
Real-robot evaluation is small and covers custom scenes and tasks only, with few tasks.
